companies.name: Ro
companies.note: A vertically integrated D2C telehealth platform covering men's health, women's health, and weight management. Currently generating ~$370M annually from GLP-1 prescriptions via partnerships with Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk.

companies.name: Hims & Hers
companies.note: A publicly traded D2C telehealth company offering treatments for sexual health, hair loss, mental health, and weight management. Competes directly with Ro in the GLP-1 market with a $499/month Wegovy offering.

companies.name: Whoop
companies.note: A wearable health monitoring platform that tracks strain, recovery, and sleep for athletes and health-conscious consumers. Expanding from performance tracking into clinical health monitoring partnerships.

companies.name: Cityblock Health
companies.note: A value-based care company focused on underserved Medicaid and low-income Medicare populations. Combines community health workers, technology, and clinical services to address social determinants of health.

companies.name: Brightline
companies.note: A behavioral health platform designed for children and teenagers, delivered through employer benefits. Provides therapy, coaching, and psychiatry for families navigating youth mental health challenges.

companies.name: Nuvation Bio
companies.note: An oncology-focused biotech using AI to identify and validate novel cancer drug targets. Focuses on multi-targeted therapies to overcome drug resistance mechanisms that limit existing treatments.

companies.name: Verve Therapeutics
companies.note: A cardiovascular gene editing company developing single-course treatments that permanently lower LDL cholesterol. Uses base editing technology pioneered at the Broad Institute to address hereditary heart disease.

companies.name: Transcarent
companies.note: An AI-powered health and benefits navigation platform serving self-insured employers. Completed a $621M merger with Accolade in April 2025, creating a combined entity serving 20M+ members across 1,700 employer and health plan clients.

companies.name: Viz.ai
companies.note: An AI-powered disease detection and care coordination platform deployed across 1,700+ hospitals globally. Specializes in time-critical conditions including stroke, pulmonary embolism, and aortic disease, and reached profitability in 2025.

companies.name: Clarify Health
companies.note: A cloud-based analytics and value-based payments platform that maps 300M+ patient journeys to generate 18B+ AI-powered predictions. Serves payers, providers, and life sciences companies with real-time clinical and financial insights.

companies.name: Anterior
companies.note: A clinician-led AI platform for health plans that automates prior authorization and payment integrity workflows. Achieved 99.24% clinical accuracy validated by KLAS Research with a deployment model built around embedded clinicians.

companies.name: Abridge
companies.note: An ambient AI documentation platform that converts patient-clinician conversations into structured clinical notes in real time. Reached a $5.3B valuation after a $300M Series E, with enterprise deployments across major US health systems.

companies.name: Isomorphic Labs
companies.note: A Google-spun-out AI drug discovery company building on AlphaFold technology to design novel therapeutics from structure prediction. Raised $600M in its first external round led by Thrive Capital.

companies.name: Lila Sciences
companies.note: A life sciences AI company building what it calls a scientific superintelligence platform for drug discovery, chemistry, and materials science. Raised $550M across three rounds in 2025, reaching a $1.3B valuation.

companies.name: Hinge Health
companies.note: A digital musculoskeletal therapy platform offering employer-sponsored programs for back, joint, and chronic pain. Filed for IPO in 2025 and is considered one of the strongest digital health public market candidates.

companies.name: Maven Clinic
companies.note: A virtual clinic specializing in women's and family health across fertility, maternity, parenting, and menopause. Serves employers and health plans with a $1.7B valuation and a growing international footprint.

companies.name: Headspace
companies.note: A merged mindfulness and mental health platform created from the combination of Headspace and Ginger. Offers both consumer wellness content and employer-sponsored clinical mental health services.

companies.name: Omada Health
companies.note: A digital chronic disease management platform focused on diabetes prevention, hypertension, and musculoskeletal health. Filed for IPO in 2025 after achieving sustainable revenue growth across employer and health plan channels.

companies.name: Aidoc
companies.note: A radiology AI platform with 23 FDA clearances covering stroke, pulmonary embolism, and incidental findings detection. Deployed across 1,000+ health systems and integrated directly into existing radiology workflows.

companies.name: Spring Health
companies.note: A precision mental health benefits platform that uses predictive analytics to match employees with the right level of care. Reached a $3.3B valuation and serves over 450 enterprise clients including Fortune 500 employers.

companies.name: Innovaccer
companies.note: A unified health data platform that aggregates and normalizes data across EHRs, claims, and clinical systems. Valued at $3.2B after a Series E, with a focus on population health management and care coordination.

companies.name: Biofourmis
companies.note: A remote patient monitoring company combining wearable biosensors with AI analytics to predict clinical deterioration. Primarily serves hospital-at-home and post-acute care programs for high-acuity patients.

companies.name: Garner Health
companies.note: An employer health benefits company that uses outcomes data to guide employees toward higher-quality providers. Incentivizes care navigation through cost-sharing rather than network restriction.

companies.name: Ambience Healthcare
companies.note: An ambient AI platform that generates real-time clinical documentation from patient-physician conversations across specialties. Designed to reduce physician burnout by eliminating after-hours charting time.

companies.name: Cohere Health
companies.note: An AI platform that automates prior authorization decisions for health plans using clinical evidence and guidelines. Focuses on reducing the administrative burden of utilization management while maintaining clinical accuracy.

companies.name: Sword Health
companies.note: A digital physical therapy platform combining AI motion technology with licensed therapists for MSK rehabilitation. Valued at $2B and serving employers and health plans across the US and Europe.

companies.name: Insilico Medicine
companies.note: An end-to-end AI drug discovery company with the first AI-designed drug to enter Phase II clinical trials. Uses generative AI across target identification, molecule design, and preclinical validation.

companies.name: BioAge Labs
companies.note: A drug discovery company using metabolomics and longitudinal human data to identify aging-related drug targets. Focuses on the biology of healthspan extension rather than individual disease indication.

companies.name: Tempus AI
companies.note: A genomics and multimodal clinical AI company that applies machine learning to molecular and clinical data to guide cancer treatment. Went public in 2024 and is one of the most capitalized digital health companies in the market.

companies.name: Hippocratic AI
companies.note: An AI company building safety-focused care agents for patient communication, education, and navigation. Designed to extend the reach of clinical teams without replacing licensed healthcare professionals.

companies.name: Suki AI
companies.note: An AI voice assistant for clinical documentation that integrates directly into EHR workflows. Reduces physician documentation time significantly and has expanded from primary care into specialty medicine.

companies.name: Neko Health
companies.note: A preventive health company offering full-body scans combining multiple imaging modalities in a single 10-minute visit. Founded by Spotify co-founder Daniel Ek, with clinics in Europe and US expansion underway.

companies.name: Oura
companies.note: A smart ring platform that tracks sleep, readiness, and health metrics for both consumer and clinical use cases. Valued at $5B with growing partnerships with health systems and insurers for population health monitoring.

companies.name: Lyra Health
companies.note: An employer mental health benefits platform providing access to evidence-based therapy and coaching through a curated provider network. One of the most capitalized mental health companies with a peak $5.58B valuation.

companies.name: Recursion
companies.note: A clinical-stage biopharma company using high-throughput biology and machine learning to decode disease biology at scale. One of the most prominent AI drug discovery companies with multiple programs in clinical development.

companies.name: Headway
companies.note: A mental health platform that helps therapists accept insurance by managing credentialing, billing, and administration. Addresses access barriers to mental health care by making insurance-covered therapy economically viable for providers.

companies.name: Waymark
companies.note: A value-based care company using technology to support community health workers in reaching high-need Medicaid patients. Focuses on trust-based longitudinal relationships rather than episodic clinical interventions.

companies.name: Arcadia
companies.note: A population health analytics platform that aggregates multi-payer data to support value-based care performance tracking. Used by health systems, ACOs, and payers to manage quality metrics and risk stratification.

companies.name: Seer Bio
companies.note: A proteomics-driven drug discovery company using deep plasma proteomics to identify novel disease biomarkers and therapeutic targets. Raised a new round in early 2026 to expand its multi-omics discovery platform.

companies.name: BioNTech Digital
companies.note: A spinout from BioNTech focused on applying mRNA platform technology and AI to oncology diagnostics and personalized cancer vaccines. One of the most closely watched digital health entrants of early 2026.

companies.name: Nym Health
companies.note: An autonomous medical coding platform using NLP to translate clinical notes into billing codes with high accuracy. Targets revenue cycle teams at hospitals and physician groups to reduce manual coding labor.

companies.name: Atropos Health
companies.note: A real-world evidence platform that generates on-demand observational studies from EHR-connected patient data. Serves pharmaceutical companies and health systems seeking rapid evidence-based answers to clinical questions.

companies.name: Nabla
companies.note: A European ambient AI documentation company expanding aggressively into the US market. Competes with Abridge and Ambience on clinical note generation quality and specialty coverage breadth.

companies.name: Heliogen Health
companies.note: An AI-powered chronic care coordination platform focused on underserved and Medicaid populations. Combines community health worker workflows with predictive analytics to reduce avoidable hospitalizations.

insights.2021: 2021 was the apex of pandemic-era digital health exuberance. Capital flooded into telehealth, consumer wearables, and D2C health platforms as remote care became normalized and investors extrapolated pandemic-era engagement permanently forward. Ro, Hims & Hers, and Whoop led a cohort defined by consumer scale and brand-driven growth. In parallel, oncology AI and gene editing attracted early deep-tech capital — a quieter signal that proved far more durable than the consumer wave.
insights.2022: 2022 brought the broadest funding environment in digital health history, with large rounds distributed across nearly every sub-sector simultaneously. Tempus AI, Lyra Health, Recursion, and Oura each raised at valuations that reflected peak market optimism. The vintage is notable for its breadth and its casualties — Forward Health and Pear Therapeutics both raised significant capital in this cohort before shutting down, illustrating the limits of scale without sustainable business models.
insights.2023: 2023 was a year of consolidation and flight to quality as the broader tech downturn compressed multiples and forced discipline. Hinge Health, Omada, and Tempus AI secured late-stage rounds signaling IPO readiness, while mental health and chronic disease management emerged as durable employer benefit categories. AI documentation began its quiet ascent — Ambience and Commure both raised in 2023, planting the seeds for the ambient AI wave that would define 2025.
insights.2024: 2024 was the year ambient clinical AI crossed from pilot to production. Abridge, Ambience, and Suki collectively raised over $800M as health systems moved decisively to enterprise contracts. Care navigation saw its defining consolidation moment — Transcarent's $621M merger with Accolade. Payer AI also matured, with Anterior and Cohere Health closing meaningful rounds on demonstrated ROI rather than promise.
insights.2025: 2025 was defined by two macro forces: the AI drug discovery supercycle and the maturation of clinical AI infrastructure. Isomorphic Labs and Lila Sciences alone absorbed over $1.1B, signaling that deep-tech life science AI has entered a new capital intensity regime. On the care delivery side, Abridge's $5.3B valuation and Hinge Health's IPO filing marked the arrival of digital health's second generation of public-market-ready companies.
insights.2026: 2026 is early but directionally clear: capital is flowing toward infrastructure, evidence, and efficiency. Proteomics, real-world evidence platforms, and autonomous coding are attracting new rounds as the market seeks the layer below the AI application stack. European ambient AI players like Nabla are entering the US market, suggesting incoming competitive pressure on domestic documentation leaders.
insights.all: Across the full dataset, capital concentration in digital health has undergone a meaningful structural shift since 2021. Early broad-market enthusiasm — characterized by large rounds into telehealth platforms and consumer wearables — has given way to targeted infrastructure-layer bets. AI-native clinical tools, ambient documentation, and payer workflow automation are absorbing the largest share of late-stage conviction capital heading into 2026. The companies commanding the highest valuations today are no longer platform plays; they are deeply integrated workflow tools with measurable ROI.
